title: 环境与健康讲座词汇
goal: 辨认环境与健康词汇；听懂相关讲述中的作用关系。

points.label: 听懂相关讲述中的作用关系

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 环境与健康词汇和听力材料规格

body.p: 环境与健康类讲述常讲暴露来源、物质循环、人体反应和预防措施。听作用关系时，要分清来源、接触途径和可能的结果。

body.box: A filter can remove some particles from the air passing through it. Its effect depends on the filter and the way air moves.

body.p: filter 是措施，particles 是处理对象。some 和 depends on 限定了作用范围。

body.box: Dust can enter a room through an open door or be carried in on clothing. A ventilation system moves air through the building. If the system includes a suitable filter, some airborne particles can be removed from the air that passes through it. The filter must be maintained, and its effect depends on the system and the particles involved. Reducing a source of dust can also reduce the amount entering the room.

body.p: Dust 是暴露来源，airborne particles 是过滤对象。some 和 depends on 限定了过滤效果。减少来源和过滤空气是两种不同的措施。

body.box:
What does the filter do in the passage?
1. It removes some particles from air passing through it.
2. It prevents every particle from entering the building.
3. It creates dust on clothing outside the building.
4. It replaces the need to maintain the ventilation system.

body.p: some airborne particles can be removed from the air that passes through it 对应第一项。

groups.fill: A community workshop collects used containers. The conta{iners} are cle{aned} and retu{rned} for re{use} by lo{cal} residents. Th{is} reduces t{he} amount o{f} waste se{nt} to a land{fill} after one use. The workshop checks each container before returning it. Damaged containers are separated from those that can be used again. The process depends on collection, inspection, and cleaning; simply gathering the containers does not make each one ready for another use.
notes: reuse：for 后的名词表示重复使用。
the：限定送往填埋场的废弃物数量。

lines.text: A workshop found dust on shelves near a cutting area. Staff first identified where the dust was produced. They then moved the cutting work to a separate area and checked the ventilation system. A filter in the system removed some particles from air passing through it. Staff also cleaned the shelves regularly. Each measure addressed a different part of the problem: separating the activity limited the spread, while cleaning removed dust already on surfaces. The staff continued to inspect the system because a filter needs maintenance.

options: On shelves near the cutting area
In the separate cutting area
On the ventilation system's filter
In air passing through the filter
items.why: dust on shelves near a cutting area 对应第一项。

items.stem: Why was cutting moved to a separate area?
options: To make the shelves easier to clean
To limit how far the dust could spread
To remove dust already on the shelves
To let the filter remove more particles
items.why: separating the activity limited the spread 说明调整位置的作用，即第二项。

options: Every particle from the air in the workshop
Dust already lying on the shelves
Some particles from air passing through it
The need to clean the shelves
items.why: removed some particles from air passing through it 对应第三项。

options: The location of the cutting activity
Air that had not passed through the system
The upkeep of the ventilation filter
Dust that had already settled on surfaces
items.why: cleaning removed dust already on surfaces 对应第四项。

items.stem: Why did staff continue to inspect the system?
options: Its filter required ongoing maintenance.
Cleaning had not removed dust from shelves.
The dust source had not been identified.
The system had eliminated every airborne particle.
items.why: a filter needs maintenance 是持续检查的原因，即第一项。

groups.fill: A school checks the quality of its indoor air. Staff mea{sure} the amo{unt} of du{st} near t{he} room's ve{nts} and rec{ord} the res{ults} over sev{eral} weeks. Th{ey} also ins{pect} the ventilation equipment regularly. Measurements describe the conditions at the time and place where they are taken. Staff compare the results with information about the room's use and check whether the equipment is working as intended. A single measurement does not describe every room or every season.

lines.text: Today we'll examine a fictional project to reduce smoke exposure in a community kitchen. Smoke can contain small particles that remain in the air. The amount people inhale depends on the source, how long they are nearby, and how the air moves. The kitchen's staff noticed that smoke sometimes gathered near the cooking area. They wanted to understand which changes might reduce the amount that reached people preparing food. Their first step was to identify the source. Smoke appeared when food was cooked at a high temperature, especially when the cooking surface was not cleaned between uses. Staff therefore adjusted their procedures and cleaned the surface regularly. This action addressed the source of some smoke rather than the air after smoke had already formed. The kitchen also had a ventilation system. Staff arranged for it to be inspected and found that one filter needed replacement. Once replaced, the filter could remove some particles from the air passing through the system. It could not remove particles from air that did not pass through it. The team checked the direction of airflow as well. A system that moves air away from the cooking area can help limit the movement of smoke toward other parts of the room. Its effect depends on the equipment and how it is used. To observe conditions, staff placed a particle monitor at a fixed location and recorded readings during similar cooking periods. They compared those readings with notes on the food being prepared and the procedures used. The readings described particles at that location and time. They did not measure exactly how much each person inhaled. Nor could one reading represent every day in the kitchen. Staff planned to repeat the observations and continue maintaining the equipment. The project distinguishes three related actions: reducing smoke at its source, moving and filtering air, and monitoring conditions. These actions work on different parts of the pathway between the source and the people nearby. A filter's presence alone does not show how well the entire system works. Inspection and repeated measurements help staff understand whether the system is operating as intended under the conditions they observe.

items.stem: What was the purpose of cleaning the cooking surface?
options: To make filter inspection unnecessary
To reduce smoke produced at its source
To filter smoke that had already formed
To measure particles in every part of the room
items.why: cleaned the surface regularly 和 addressed the source of some smoke 对应第二项。

items.stem: What could the replaced filter remove?
options: Every particle that formed in the cooking area
Particles in air that bypassed the system
The smoke at its source on the surface
Some particles in air going through the system
items.why: remove some particles from the air passing through the system 对应第四项。

items.stem: Why did staff examine the direction of airflow?
options: To see how moving air could limit the spread of smoke
To establish that filters remove particles from every location
To find where the smoke was first produced
To check whether the filter needed replacing
items.why: moves air away from the cooking area can help limit the movement of smoke 对应第一项。

items.stem: What did the monitor readings describe?
options: Exactly how much each person inhaled during the project
Every day's conditions throughout the whole kitchen
Particles at that spot during the recorded periods
The amount of smoke produced by every cooking surface
items.why: The readings described particles at that location and time 对应第三项。

items.stem: Why did staff plan repeated observations?
options: A single reading fully represented every day.
Conditions could vary across different cooking periods.
Staff had not yet replaced the old filter.
The monitor directly measured each person's inhalation.
items.why: one reading 不能代表 every day，重复观察有助于了解不同时间的情况，即第二项。
